subject: chemistry
title: Acids & Bases Adventure 1: Brønsted-Lowry and pH
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Brønsted-Lowry acids/bases and calculate pH.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — Brønsted-Lowry, conjugate pairs, pH = -log[H⁺], Kw.
final_note: You learned acids donate H⁺, bases accept; conjugate pairs differ by one proton; pH = -log[H⁺]; Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acid: donates H⁺. Base: accepts H⁺.

HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻.
- HCl/Cl⁻ is one conjugate pair.
- H₂O/H₃O⁺ is the other.

Substances can be both: H₂O is amphiprotic (HCl gives H₃O⁺; NH₃ leaves OH⁻).

Water self-ionises: 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻.

Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K.

pH = -log[H⁺]; pOH = -log[OH⁻]. pH + pOH = 14 at 298 K.

Pure water: [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷; pH = 7. Acidic < 7, basic > 7.

Strong acids dissociate fully: HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄. [H⁺] = [acid].

Weak acids partial: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺. [H⁺] < [acid].

0.10 mol/dm³ HCl: pH = 1.
0.10 mol/dm³ CH₃COOH (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵): pH ≈ 2.9.
